rv.q: In Brigid Larmour’s finely etched production, irritable passions ferment beneath the frowsty knits and beads.
This is a wonderful revival of a marvellous play.
This pleasingly grown-up play depends on words, suggestion and action rather than gimmickry.
The play ends on a note of high anxiety, its plot lines fruitfully unresolved, but with its dramatic potential underachieved.
As the catalyst for unpleasantness however, Ms Thaw oft seen broodingly catatonic in a rocking chair, seems slightly miscast and too young to play the sinister and crotchety battle-axe.
The Old Ladies really is a creaky old piece of theatre.
There is little depth or shading to the characters.
This is a Rodney Ackland revival, well worth it, the Finborough always does these forgotten-plays with great class.

cn.t: Period thriller from 1935 receives mixed reviews, with critics divided on whether it has aged well. Some praise its atmospheric character study of lonely, impoverished women, while others find the plot tame and dated by modern standards.
